name: FDA approves generic hormone therapy patch
summary: The US FDA approved the first generic version of the Climara Pro once-weekly patch, which combines estradiol and levonorgestrel, on 20 October 2026.
keyPoints: The US FDA approved the first generic of Climara Pro on 20 October 2026.
Climara Pro is a once-weekly patch containing estradiol and levonorgestrel for women with an intact uterus.
The FDA describes the generic as therapeutically equivalent to the brand product.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
On 20 October 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first generic version of Climara Pro.

Climara Pro is a transdermal patch, worn for a week at a time, that contains estradiol and levonorgestrel and is for women with an intact uterus.

The FDA describes the generic as therapeutically equivalent to the brand product.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The FDA says the progestogen in the patch is there to reduce the risk of endometrial hyperplasia, which can occur with oestrogen alone.

The agency presented the approval as a way to widen access to medicines.

This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.

source.title: FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women
